items.stem: According to the Born rule, the quantity that gives the probability density of finding a particle at a point is

options.text: the squared magnitude of the wavefunction
options.rationale: Correct: |psi|^2 is the probability density in the Born interpretation.
The wavefunction can be complex and is not a probability.
Energy does not give a spatial probability density.
The derivative relates to momentum, not probability density.

items.explanation: Correct: |psi|^2 is the probability density in the Born interpretation.

items.stem: Which TWO phenomena cannot be explained by classical physics and require quantum mechanics? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Electrons tunnelling through a potential barrier they lack the energy to cross classically
options.rationale: Correct: tunnelling is a purely quantum effect.

options.text: The discrete emission spectrum of atomic hydrogen
options.rationale: Correct: discrete spectral lines reflect quantised energy levels.

options.text: A ball rolling down a frictionless ramp
options.rationale: This is well described by classical mechanics.

options.text: The parabolic path of a thrown stone

items.explanation: Correct: tunnelling is a purely quantum effect.

items.stem: The energy levels of a particle confined to an infinite square well are quantised because

options.text: only wavelengths that fit an integer number of half-wavelengths in the well are allowed
options.rationale: Correct: boundary conditions select discrete standing-wave modes, giving quantised energies.

options.text: the particle loses energy to the walls
options.rationale: The walls are idealised and do no work; quantisation comes from boundary conditions.

options.text: the particle is always at rest
options.rationale: A confined particle has nonzero minimum (zero-point) energy.

options.text: energy is continuous but we can only measure discrete values
options.rationale: The allowed energies themselves are discrete for a bound system.

items.explanation: Correct: boundary conditions select discrete standing-wave modes, giving quantised energies.
